modes.title: Intent classification errors
modes.scope: LLM classifier (gpt-oss-120b) on the 100 blind-human golden cases

examples.message: So @VirginTrains got a new voice in the toilets. Shit myself not in the place I’d planned to.
examples.detail: gold `chitchat_non_support`, predicted `journey_disruption_complaint` (confidence 0.92)

examples.message: Hey @VirginTrains I’m sure the automated voice in your loos is fun and quirky to most folk.....unless they have a heart condition!!!!
examples.detail: gold `customer_service_complaint`, predicted `chitchat_non_support` (confidence 0.97)

examples.message: London bound @VirginTrains 💞 #HappySunday https://t.co/l3O7CMWdXb
examples.detail: gold `praise_positive_feedback`, predicted `chitchat_non_support` (confidence 0.97)

modes.observed: 40 of 100 blind cases misclassified; 32 of those errors had self-reported confidence >= 0.90, so the confidence threshold (0.75) does not catch them.
modes.why: Self-reported LLM confidence is uncalibrated; the classifier sees only the opening tweet while the labeler saw the whole conversation.
modes.fix: Calibrate confidence on dev (reliability curve) or replace it with retrieval-agreement signals; give the classifier the thread context the labeler had.

modes.title: Intent boundary ambiguity
modes.scope: LLM errors on the blind 100, grouped into unordered intent pairs

examples.message: @VirginTrains Hello I'm on the 18:15 from Birmingham to edinburgh there has been a few announcements but I can't hear any of them because of a lot of…
examples.detail: gold `journey_disruption_complaint`, predicted `service_status_delay_enquiry`; label confidence high

examples.message: @VirginTrains running late from London - probably not their fault. But then abandoned Shropshire passengers in Wolverhampton. Poor show.
examples.detail: gold `service_status_delay_enquiry`, predicted `journey_disruption_complaint`; label confidence high

examples.message: @VirginTrains any idea how long the Euston line will be blocked for?
examples.detail: gold `journey_disruption_complaint`, predicted `service_status_delay_enquiry`; label confidence medium

modes.observed: Most confused pairs: journey_disruption_complaint / service_status_delay_enquiry (5); chitchat_non_support / praise_positive_feedback (4); service_status_delay_enquiry / ticket_booking_query (3); customer_service_complaint / ticket_booking_query (2). Independently, the candidate taxonomy disagrees with the final gold intent on 131 of 250 golden cases.
modes.why: Several intents describe the same tweet from different angles (a delayed train is both a status question and a complaint); the taxonomy came from soft clusters (silhouette about 0.05).
modes.fix: Define intents by the action the brand must take (live info / compensation / acknowledge) and add decision rules for the top pairs; re-label only after freezing the new definitions.

modes.title: Retrieval finds the topic but not the handling
modes.scope: proxy retrieval evaluation on 857 dev queries (labels are heuristic, not human)

examples.message: Hi @VirginTrains on what planet can you justify this price? Will I have my own private carriage, hand-waited on by Tom Hardy? 🙃
examples.detail: proxy relevance = same intent `chitchat_non_support` + resolution `troubleshooting`; top-1 was `first_class_catering_issue` / `information_provided`; first relevant at rank 47

examples.message: Dear @VirginTrains, whilst I really appreciate your on average 2 hour service for London Euston to Manchester Piccadilly, I would also love for you t…
examples.detail: proxy relevance = same intent `praise_positive_feedback` + resolution `self_service`; top-1 was `praise_positive_feedback` / `feedback_acknowledged`; first relevant at rank 9

examples.message: trying to get to Birmingham now can I use virgin from Watford with this??
examples.detail: proxy relevance = same intent `service_status_delay_enquiry` + resolution `refund`; top-1 was `service_status_delay_enquiry` / `information_provided`; first relevant at rank 246

modes.observed: 185 queries had no relevant case in the top 5; 178 of them retrieved the same intent but a different resolution type.
modes.why: The opening message rarely contains what decided the historical handling (ticket type, eligibility, whether a DM happened).
modes.fix: Retrieve on the full thread when available and show resolution-type diversity in the evidence instead of top-5 by similarity alone.

modes.title: Over-escalation built into the policy
modes.scope: hard rules applied to the GOLD intent of the blind 100 (perfect-classifier oracle)

examples.message: @VirginTrains chaos at Euston. My sister was told to go to Marylebone, but then her train departed almost on time. How to get a refund?
examples.detail: gold intent `delay_repay_refund_claim`, gold should_escalate = no; fired: intent rule (delay_repay_refund_claim); sensitive wording (refund)

examples.message: @VirginTrains Just had a lovely journey on the 0930 Euston to Glasgow, got off at Lancaster. James at Euston and Katie the train manager were very he…
examples.detail: gold intent `praise_positive_feedback`, gold should_escalate = no; fired: sensitive wording (wheelchair)

examples.message: Hey @VirginTrains I’m sure the automated voice in your loos is fun and quirky to most folk.....unless they have a heart condition!!!!
examples.detail: gold intent `customer_service_complaint`, gold should_escalate = no; fired: intent rule (customer_service_complaint)

modes.observed: Of 81 blind cases a human said need not escalate, 40 would still be escalated by a hard rule even with perfect classification (intent rule 37, sensitive wording 7, low-information 1; a case can fire several).
modes.why: Whole intents are blocked (status, disruption, Delay Repay, complaints, unclear), and the sensitive-word list matches words like 'wheelchair' or 'refund' even in praise or simple questions.
modes.fix: Gate on the action needed rather than the intent (a timetable question is not a live-status question), and scope sensitive words to complaints; tune on dev, not golden.

modes.title: Potential unsafe auto-handles

examples.message: @VirginTrains @127472 you’ve just tried charging me £102 to change my ticket from 13:30 nom peak train from London to Lancaster to 11:30 non peak tra…
examples.detail: gold intent `ticket_booking_query`, gold should_escalate = yes; no hard rule fires; note: -

examples.message: Great work @VirginTrains no buffet or trolley service on a 3hr journey? Even @121513 can sort that shit out #shambles
examples.detail: gold intent `first_class_catering_issue`, gold should_escalate = yes; no hard rule fires; note: -

examples.message: @VirginTrains your cross country to Plymouth this evening was late but to be fair it was (thank god) warm and the staff on it were lush.
examples.detail: gold intent `praise_positive_feedback`, gold should_escalate = yes; no hard rule fires; note: -

modes.observed: 3 of 19 blind cases that should escalate are not caught by any hard rule; only the soft checks (confidence, evidence, grounding) stand between them and an auto-reply. Observed in the agent run: 1 of 50 scored cases auto-handled although gold says escalate (case_2884600).
modes.why: Escalation-worthy cases that look like routine intents (e.g. a booking question that actually needs an account lookup) slip past intent-level rules.
modes.fix: Measure auto-handle precision on the full 50-case slice, then add the specific triggers found (account/booking-reference requests) as rules.

modes.why: See the policy oracle above: most are blanket intent rules or sensitive words.
modes.fix: Same as the policy oracle fix.

modes.title: Reply-generation failures

examples.message: Nothing quite as #discombobulating as hearing #WillFerrell's voice as you sit down on a @VirginTrains #train #toilet. #TGIF #DaddysHome2
examples.detail: generation = declined

modes.observed: 1 of 15 attempted generations declined or errored.
modes.why: Generator refuses when evidence does not cover the question, or the model output is unusable.
modes.fix: Inspect declined drafts once the full run exists.

examples.detail: unsupported: Advance fares for that route are released about 12 weeks before travel; typically around 24 October for a 13 January jou

examples.detail: unsupported: The onboard team can provide the most up‑to‑date information on payment options.

modes.observed: 3 of 14 grounding checks failed or could not run.
modes.why: Drafts add details (times, links, promises) the evidence does not contain.
modes.fix: Keep fail-closed; report blocked drafts alongside sent ones.

examples.detail: weak retrieval: best similarity 0.58 < 0.60; insufficient evidence: 1 usable case(s) < 3; evidence disagrees with the predicted intent: 0% of usable cases share

modes.observed: 16 of 50 cases had weak, too few or intent-inconsistent evidence.
modes.why: Rare or unusual complaints have no close historical match in the train split.
modes.fix: Expected behaviour (abstain); track how often it is the only reason for escalation.

modes.title: Cases involving another train operator
modes.scope: all 250 golden cases (thread data + label notes)

examples.message: @VirginTrains what is going on with the heating on the 13.00 Edinburgh - LKX???
examples.detail: note: Heating complaint on another operator's service; redirected to them.

examples.message: This is how you travel by virgin now !!!!! Shame on you @VirginTrains https://t.co/cLAdWmk2Hj
examples.detail: note: Overcrowding on another operator's service; redirected to them.

examples.message: Now I’ve got #280characters probably a good time to continue my story. Also delayed massively by @VirginTrains so let’s be honest I have some time!
examples.detail: note: Delay on another operator's service.

modes.observed: 19 golden cases either have another operator's agent in the thread or a label note saying the service was another operator's (5 of them in the blind 100).
modes.why: Customers tag VirginTrains about trains it does not run; the right answer is a redirect, which no intent captures.
modes.fix: Add an operator-detection rule (station/route and operator names) and a 'redirect to operator' resolution path.

modes.title: Low-information and media-only messages

examples.message: @VirginTrains can you help? X https://t.co/abcXynNhtz
examples.detail: gold `unclear_or_media_only`; LLM predicted `unclear_or_media_only`

examples.message: @VirginTrains to Edinburgh Haymarket? 2.
examples.detail: gold `unclear_or_media_only`; LLM predicted `service_status_delay_enquiry`

examples.message: @VirginTrains your trains are disgusting.... https://t.co/vnZr1Pf8bH
examples.detail: gold `unclear_or_media_only`; LLM predicted `journey_disruption_complaint`

modes.observed: 7 cases are gold `unclear_or_media_only`; the LLM labelled 2 of them as unclear. Opening messages with fewer than 3 content words (which the policy escalates): 1.
modes.why: The real request is in an image or a link the system never sees, so the model guesses an intent from the surrounding words.
modes.fix: Treat bare links/images as an explicit low-information trigger and ask a clarifying question instead of classifying.
